correctness.rationale: For compact self-adjoint B-cI, infinitely many below-c eigenvalues contradict the well-ordering condition of Golla–Osaka–Sequeira Theorem 2.2. A top-(r+n) negative-eigenspace of D intersects the codimension-r nonnegative spectral subspace of B in dimension at least n; there the quadratic form of B-D is bounded below by kappa_(r+n). Compact self-adjoint min–max gives the singular bound. Clipping all but m negative eigenvalues yields a positive beta(H) operator with exact error tail; Schatten conclusions follow by summation, including noncommuting B and p<1. Package verify.py passed 27 finite supplementary tests. No unproved infinite-dimensional estimate is inferred from numerical experiments.

originality.rationale: The novel candidate is not positive beta(H) well-ordering, scalar-plus-compact AN structure, or ordinary norm density. It is the sharp all-n lower singular-value comparison against arbitrary noncommuting positive beta(H) corrections with bounded subthreshold multiplicity, together with a single sharp optimizer for all n and the exact one-sided Schatten-p repair characterization. The full text of the motivating paper does not state these inequalities or the finite-exception variational optimization. Closest published published-finding corpus summary concerns operator-norm distance and nearest points, neither of which dominates the all-rank Schatten statement. Relevant partial-isometry Schatten and beta_0 stability papers could not be inspected beyond abstracts; their overlap remains an explicit residual risk.
